 The cast of Yu-Gi-Oh! GX is coming back in 2027, and Konami has featured these iconic duelists in a debut gameplay trailer ahead of their February 16 return.

 The Yu-Gi-Oh! franchise took a multimedia approach, with characters from the anime using cards that would appear in the tabletop game. This meant that the series had a cyclical approach, meaning the likes of Yugi and Kaiba from the first era would be phased out, only returning for the video games or the occasional nostalgia return, like The Dark Side of Dimensions movie.
 Yu-Gi-Oh Tag Force GX Debut Trailer Features Iconic Characters
 Yu-Gi-Oh! GX ended its run in 2008, but the attendees of the Duel Academy are coming back in 2027 . Yu-Gi-Oh! Tag Force GX is an upcoming remake of Yu-Gi-Oh! GX Tag Force 3 that's set to launch on PC, Nintendo Switch, and Nintendo Switch 2 on February 16, 2027.
 The official Yu-Gi-Oh! EU YouTube channel has uploaded the debut gameplay trailer for Yu-Gi-Oh! Tag Force GX , featuring the returning characters, and showing off the new features that have been included. As the name suggests, Yu-Gi-Oh! Tag Force GX is all about 2v2 duels. 
 Players have their own customizable avatar character with a deck that they build themselves, but they need to team up with another student at the Duel Academy to participate in games. This means the player can form teams with the likes of Jaden Yuki, Alexis Rhodes, Chazz Princeton, Bastion Misawa, and Zane Truesdale, as they duel their way to the top.

 What's New In Yu-Gi-Oh! Tag Force GX
 Image Via Konami 
 Yu-Gi-Oh! Tag Force GX has improved the visuals from the original version of the game, including the overworld, dueling field, and the special cinematics that play when iconic creatures are summoned. Brand-new cards from the Yu-Gi-Oh! GX era have been added, including Rainbow NEOS, while extra mini games have been added for people who want to bond with their classmates.
 There's also a new online mode for people who want to Tag Duel with their friends. Yu-Gi-Oh! GX existed in an era before Yu-Gi-Oh! started adding new summoning methods to the game, as it still heavily relied on mechanics from the first series.
 Yu-Gi-Oh! GX also, arguably, had a lighter tone than its predecessor and successor, which is why people have such strong nostalgia for it. Those who want to relive their glory days can do so next year, when Yu-Gi-Oh! Tag Force GX arrives, and the doors of the Duel Academy open once more.
